messages:
frank: Quick sync on the Aphelion9b bring-up. Ran our static int4 pack on ded-3. Short-ctx QA looks OK but long summaries start looping after ~1800 tokens. Also saw weird kv-resume mismatch when prefixing with system messages.

maya: repro command I used:
```bash
./eval_runner --model hf/aphelion9b-v1 --quant static-int4 --prompts tests/long_summaries.txt --max-tokens 4096 --warmup 1 --batch 1
```

cheng: did you run the vocab converter with normalization? some upstream releases keep U+200B and soft-hyphen, which shifts token ids for composite tokens.

frank: converter run used `hf-convert --preserve-norm` to match upstream exactly. suspect that preserved zero-width causing id offsets in range 4096..4110.

maya: small test: strip U+200B before encode -> repeats reduced. shim I used:
```py
def encode_shim(text):
    return tok.encode(text.replace('\u200B',''))
```

cheng: interesting — that would cause token boundary shifts and could make rotary positions misalign with cached KV slices.

frank: also tried toggling KV warmup. `--kvmode=warmup` reduces loop frequency, `--kvmode=stateless` brings it back. So warmup seems to mask, not fix.

sanjay: I ran `rotary-inspect` and found fractional phase offsets on two heads (tiny):
```
head 4 offset=+0.0625
head 11 offset=-0.03125
```
Could be byteorder or quant pack alignment. Cheng, did we change pack stride recently?

cheng: last pack change was fused-int4 alignment tweak on 3/2026. We avoided per-head scales for that run. If packing shifted low-level byte layout, it could affect dequant in projection tensors and produce tiny phase drift.

maya: plan: 1) run converter with NFKC + remove zero-widths and re-pack; 2) rerun generation with force warmup flag to see residual; 3) if still failing, rebuild pack with per_head_scale=true and compare per-head checksums.

frank: created a quick mapping diff that fixes the 4096 region by collapsing zero-width variants -> will run eval after queue (~12m).

ops-bot: Created ticket RH-2421: "Aphelion9b: int4 onboarding - token id offsets + kv warmup mismatch + tiny rotary head offsets" assigned eng-ml. https://redwood.example/issue/RH-2421

cheng: priority order agrees with plan. tokenizer first (fast), kv warmup/runtime flags second (instrumented), pack-rebuild last (takes infra time).

frank: attaching minimal checksum run for deterministic LM-step (seeded):
```bash
python -c "from runner import Model; m=Model('hf/aphelion9b-v1'); print(m.step_checksum(seed=1337, steps=8))"
# output: projU_checksum=ab12cd34 projV_checksum=12ef34ab kv_init=00112233
```

maya: thanks — I'll diff those against golden and post results after converter rerun.

frank: thanks all, will update when eval finishes. :hourglass:
